subject: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request

Team —

Short ask: Helios (enterprise pilot) wants a short-lived, non-preemptible slice for their pilot window. We need to evaluate whether we can grant an exception to the standard autoscale/preemption policy and reserve capacity for two weeks. Details below.

What Helios is asking for
- Window: 2026-06-22 00:00 UTC -> 2026-07-06 23:59 UTC (14 days)
- Preferred region: eu-west-1
- Model: orca-enterprise-v2 (fp16), roughly 3B params quantized fallback available
- Expected baseline: ~12 steady QPS (inference v1), bursts to 40 QPS for 30–90s
- Hard requirement from customer: no preemption during the window (customer cannot tolerate mid-epoch interruptions for their integration tests)

Our ask to infra/SRE
- Can we carve out a temporary reserved slice (non-preemptible) for the window? Target size: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent capacity)
- If non-preemptible full reservation is not possible, list fallbacks we can offer (guaranteed baseline + ephemeral burst; warm cache strategy; model quantization suggestions)
- Ops ask: an ops playbook (warmers, circuit breaker thresholds, runbook for graceful degrade) and a single-point oncall for the window

Attachments: pilot_runbook.pdf (customer-facing runbook), traffic_estimate.xlsx (QPS curves)
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/contacts/HLX-4721

Customer context: Helios is an active prospect in late-stage procurement. Aditya is managing the deal; they expect the pilot to prove latency/consistency before signing a 12-month Dedicated contract.

Can we get a quick feasibility note and preferred fallback by EOD today? I know this is tight.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: pilot_runbook.pdf (application/pdf)
-- Attachment: traffic_estimate.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request

Thanks for the heads up, Kim. Quick read-through below and an initial operational proposal.

Reality check
- eu-west-1 capacity is moderately constrained that week (several pilots + two enterprise ramps). I can’t promise a full 6 non-preemptible A100-equivalent carveout without displacing existing commitments.

Operational proposal (preferred)
- Reserve a guaranteed baseline of 3 GPUs for the entire window (non-preemptible) + enable an ephemeral burst lane of up to 6 additional preemptible GPUs for sustained bursts.
- Autoscale suggestion: min=3, target=6, max=12 for the slice. We'll implement an eviction grace period of 10 minutes for preemptible nodes so in-flight requests can fail gracefully.
- Canary cadence: 6/22 (canary start, 10 users), 6/23 (50 users), 6/24 (full pilot) — we’ll block the ephemeral lane for canary traffic only.

If Helios requires absolute no-preemption for the full 6 GPUs, we need budget approval to reserve the capacity (we’d need to pull from reserved pool commitments or offer a temporary paid carveout). If they are open to partial preemption we can avoid displacing other commitments.

Next steps
- I’ll file CAP-3421 to track the exception and capacity carve (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CAP-3421).
- Marcus, can you confirm whether a 3+ephemeral approach is operationally feasible and outline any additional runbook items?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 16:50:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request

I agree with Jonas' assessment — eu-west is tight. A few additional operational constraints and a concrete fallback plan: 

Constraints
- We have two other reserved commitments overlapping that week; pulling a full 6 non-preemptible will require re-negotiation with other internal stakeholders or a short-term capacity buy (cost center approval).
- Eviction of preemptible nodes currently is best-effort; making them "graceful" requires a short-running queueer and quicker KV cache flushes.

Fallback plan (what we can guarantee with low risk)
1) Guaranteed baseline: 4 GPUs non-preemptible in eu-west-1 for the window
2) Ephemeral burst lane: additional 4 preemptible GPUs (max burst) with an eviction grace of 10m and explicit circuit-breaker on token/latency budget
3) Warmers & KV cache: We'll prepare a warmers job to populate KV cache 30 minutes before canary start; also recommend batching policy change for the pilot (lower batch sizes to keep p99 latency predictable)
4) Ops playbook attached: ops_playbook.md — includes rollback steps, cloud-provider contact, and runbook owner assignment

If Helios demands 6 guaranteed non-preemptible GPUs we can do it but only if sales funds a short-term reservation or we shift other pilots. That will add procurement time and likely delay the start by 48–72 hours.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: ops_playbook.md (text/markdown)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request

Quick update from the customer side — I had a call with Margo (Helios) this morning. Key points: 
- Helios' integration tests will run overnight during the first three days of the pilot; they want deterministic behavior.
- They are willing to accept a hybrid arrangement (guaranteed baseline + burst) if we can give an operational guarantee that their canary runs will not be preempted. They asked for a written note that the canary window will use only the guaranteed capacity.
- Procurement: they want DocuSign for a short-term paid carveout if they have to pay for non-preemptible capacity.

Deal metadata: HLX-4721 (please reference in CAP ticket)
DocuSign (procurement): https://docusign.com/HLX-4721/pilot-carveout

If infra can guarantee 4 non-preemptible GPUs and promise the canary windows will be fully served from those 4 for the first 72 hours, Helios can proceed without an upfront carveout payment. Otherwise they will pay for 6 guaranteed GPUs for the 2-week window.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 18:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Helios pilot: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request

Thanks everyone — summary and agreed plan below so we have a single source of truth. I’ll own communication to Helios once the infra playbook and CAP ticket exist.

Agreed carveout (final)
- Reserve 4 non-preemptible GPUs in eu-west-1 for 2026-06-22 -> 2026-07-06 (guaranteed baseline)
- Provide an ephemeral burst lane up to 4 additional preemptible GPUs (max burst = 8 total)
- Autoscale policy for slice: min=4, target=6, max=8 for the pilot window
- Canary protection: 6/22–6/24 (first 72 hours) will be routed exclusively to the guaranteed 4 GPUs; ephemeral lane will be blocked for canary traffic

Operational items & owners
- CAP-3421 created by Jonas (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CAP-3421) — tracks approvals, costs, and provisioning (Jonas owner)
- Ops playbook (Marcus) — attach runbook and warmers; ensure eviction grace timers and circuit-breaker thresholds are in the playbook (Marcus owner)
- Sales/procurement (Aditya) — hold DocuSign link; if Helios insists on 6 guaranteed GPUs we escalate to finance for a short-term paid carveout (Aditya owner)
- Product (Laura) — confirm the model config & batching guidance for pilot (Laura owner)

Artifacts attached: pilot_runbook.pdf, traffic_estimate.xlsx, ops_playbook.md
Related links: CAP-3421, HubSpot record HLX-4721, Drive folder with pilot artefacts

Immediate next steps (today)
1) Jonas to confirm provisioning timeline (ETA for reserved slice) + file CAP ticket (Jonas)
2) Marcus to finalize ops_playbook.md and provide runbook owner + warmers schedule (Marcus)
3) Aditya to confirm Helios acceptance of the 4+ephemeral plan and to hold DocuSign if needed (Aditya)

I’ll send the customer note after Jonas confirms the CAP ticket and timeline (likely tomorrow morning). Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
